overview.overview:
New Mexico has voted Democratic in every presidential election since 2008, though its margin narrowed from 10.79 points in 2020 to 6.0 points in 2024. The state still leans about 7 points more Democratic than the nation as a whole, and the expected margin for 2028 is 12.1 points, with an 80 percent range running from 2.9 to 21.1 points.

With 5 electoral votes, New Mexico is unlikely to be decisive: the estimated odds that it becomes the tipping-point state are well under one percent. Its outcome will most likely follow the national environment rather than drive it.
overview.watch: A continued shift toward Republicans in the Albuquerque area and along the southern border could bring New Mexico back into competitive range.
key_factors: A strong Democratic lean of about 7 points relative to the nation
A narrowing trend, with the 2024 margin roughly half of the 2020 margin
Only 5 electoral votes and minimal tipping-point relevance
